Cooling 14% Plug Loads 28% Cooling for Fresh Air 14% Lighting Heating 12% 13% Hot Water Heating for Fresh Air 6% 13% Figure 3: Energy Use by Category for Sample Building Activity The audit identified 34 options for improving the building’s energy use as well as calculated energy impacts and capital costs for the retrofit options. Each of these measures is identified on the color-coded cards. Your task, as a building owner team, is to select a card from each category (i.e., one card of each color) and determine a total retrofit “package” for the building. Note that each category has a card that represents no change to the building. Each card contains information about the measure’s contribution to building energy loads, the capital cost of implementing that measure, and the savings achieved by that measure (expressed in terms of payback period). Some cards also include special multipliers or other considerations. Please note that the energy metrics on the cards do not represent savings, but rather contributions to the building’s energy use in each category. For each color family, the “do nothing” card is the base. Savings are the difference between a retrofit card and the “do nothing” card. 6 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. Step 1: Consider Options and Goals Using the Overview Table (1.3), write down your goals. Below are examples of potential goals for this activity: - Is your goal to have the best payback (i.e. best return based on the money invested)? - Are you aiming to achieve the lowest possible EUI? - Do you want to determine a set energy savings level, such as a 50% reduction from the baseline? - How disruptive will the retrofit be to the building occupants? Is that an important consideration to your team? Step 2: Examine Activity Cards Review the activity Game Cards (1.4) and discuss the retrofit measures with your team. Each card indicates a particular strategy to be applied to the building and provides information on how it will contribute to energy loads, how much it will cost, and how long it will take to pay back the investment with savings. EUI values provided on each card specify how much that measure will contribute to building loads in each category.
